To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
self-assembled stacks consisting of manganese porphyin trimers catalyse the photocatalytic oxidation of olefins with high activity and stereoselectivity.

the self-assembled trimeric Mn porphyrin complexes are efficient photocatalysts for the epoxidation of olefins with O2 as the terminal oxidant, and that the supramolecular structure leads to increased stability and stereoselectivity in the reaction.
The self-assembled stacks are highly efficient in the photocatalysis of stilbene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalytic systems based on the use of supramolecular assemblies of transition metal complexes.
the synthesis of supramolecular systems for photocatalysis.
the design and development of new supramolecular structures that exhibit enhanced catalytic activity in the oxidation of organic substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supramolecular structure leads to increased stability and enhances the stereoelectronic selectivity of the system.
the catalytic activity of the catalyst is a function of the supramolecular structure, and the stereoselectivty is a function of both the supramolecular assembly and the nature of the catalyst.
self-assembled stacks exhibit high catalytic activity, high stereoselectivity, and high stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of self-assembled porphyrin stacks as photocatalysts in organic synthesis is a very promising approach.
the self-assembled stacks are very efficient catalysts in the epoxidation of alkenes with O2 as oxidant.
we have developed a new class of catalysts based on self-assembled stacks.

the supramolecular organization of the catalysts can have a significant impact on the catalytic activity of a reaction.
